strengths: The central proposal is well motivated under the stated causal assumptions. Learning a PAG over interpretable features and predictions provides an appropriate way to represent uncertainty about causal ancestry when relevant features are unobserved.

The distinction between pixel-level inputs and macro-level explanatory concepts is useful and has an identifiable audience in explainability, causal discovery, and algorithm auditing. Applying established causal discovery tools to this problem can constitute a valuable contribution.

The manuscript clearly explains its focus on population-level explanations and discusses important limitations involving background knowledge, feature availability, and partial identification. The simulation and two applications make the workflow concrete, with substantial implementation and preprocessing details in the appendices.
weaknesses: Necessary: Address selection bias in the X-ray experiment. Section 6.1 selects pneumonia cases and controls with 'no findings,' so inclusion depends on diagnosis and the explanatory findings. This selection mechanism is outside the model that treats selection bias as irrelevant in Section 3. Under selection, PAG endpoint interpretations do not automatically establish the causal ancestry claimed here. An appropriate sampling or selection analysis is needed, or the clinical results must be substantially narrowed to an illustrative analysis without validated causal interpretations.

Necessary: Align the empirical conclusions with PAG semantics. Figure 8 pools definite and possible causes, although a possible-cause edge can also represent confounding without a causal effect. Bootstrap frequency measures stability, not the probability or magnitude of a causal effect. Furthermore, absence of adjacency to the prediction does not exclude an indirect causal path through another feature. Statements in Section 6.4 and the figure captions that particular attributes are important causes while others are not causally relevant therefore exceed the reported evidence. Report definite and possible ancestry separately and qualify the negative conclusions.

Necessary: Establish the adequacy of the conditional-independence testing. With 26 multicategory bird attributes and conditioning sets of size up to four, sparse contingency tables are a substantial concern; the 240-image X-ray analysis also involves potentially rare findings. The manuscript provides no diagnostics showing that the chi-square approximations are reliable. Report the actual discovery sample, handling of sparse cells, and sensitivity to relevant testing and search settings. Also clarify whether discovery uses training or held-out predictions and whether repeated patients enter the X-ray analysis.

Necessary: Correct or redefine the Shapley example in Section 3.3 and Appendix A. In A.1, coalition calculations retain the observational distribution of Z1 when intervening on Z2 or Z3, despite their causal effects on Z1 in the stated SCM. These quantities therefore do not generally equal the SCM's intervention means. In A.2, the allegedly omitted Z3 remains fixed inside the calculation rather than being integrated through its conditional distribution. The comparison does not establish the asserted failure of a well-defined adjustment-based estimator as written. Specify the intervention and coalition estimands consistently and rederive the example.

Necessary: Substantiate the simulation's claimed causal ground truth. Appendix B reports imperfect shape detectors and nonzero circle and triangle coefficients. Hard thresholding can eliminate those coefficients' influence on the final class when the detector outputs are binary, but this does not establish that changing circles or triangles leaves the learned horizontal and vertical detectors unchanged. Clarify the prediction representation and verify invariance through controlled shape interventions, or explicitly qualify the simulation as an approximation to the asserted causal graph.

Optional improvement: A comparison using the same concept annotations, such as an associational baseline on the controlled simulation, would better isolate the benefit of accounting for latent confounding. The LIME and SHAP examples primarily demonstrate differences in explanatory representation and do not independently validate the causal accuracy of the proposed explanations.
